title: Runtime leads briefing snapshot 2027-06-08
content:
Context:
Short-form capture from the cross-team runtime leads weekly. Focus was planning for next quarter capacity, a lightweight performance experiment summary, and a few pressing SRE asks. This was not intended as the final write-up, more as an actionable snapshot for owners.

Attendees:
- Ethan Morales (hosting runtime lead, chair)
- Maya Singh (platform capacity)
- Oliver Chen (SRE - autoscale & deployments)
- Ruth Alvarez (observability & telemetry)
- Samir Patel (product - dedicated offerings)
- Guests: Irene Park (solutions eng - customer readiness)

Duration: 45 minutes

Topline items (2 min each):
- Capacity: Maya reports projected 28% growth in reserved dedicated usage next quarter driven by two mid-market accounts reaching pilot. Need ~24 A100-equivalent slots extra to keep headroom.
- Stability: Oliver: steady error rates but an uptick in transient RPC errors during scale events.
- Metrics: Ruth: new wide-card tracing shows 0.6% of requests account for 14% of tail CPU time.

Discussion highlights:
1) Quarter-ahead capacity plan and short-term levers (15m)
- Proposal: defer one non-critical infra migration to free immediate capacity; negotiate trial credits with one of the pilot customers to smooth ramp.
- Decision: approve temporary borrowing of 12 slots from non-prod cluster while new capacity orders complete. Maya to author a rollback plan for reclaiming those slots.
- Risk: borrowing reduces non-prod test coverage for nightly stress tests; Oliver will schedule a condensed test window.

2) Performance experiment summary: packed vs loose batcher (10m)
- Experiment: compared "packed" (aggressive fill) vs "loose" (latency-priority) batching on internal T5-like workload with 4k context.
- Results: packed gave 19% token-cost reduction but increased 95th latency by ~46ms for short prompts. Loose preserves P95 but cost rises ~11%.
- Implication: mixed traffic customers should default to loose unless explicitly cost-sensitive; product should expose this as routing preference.
- Action: Samir to draft proposal for an SDK flag and runtime routing key (owner: Samir Patel, due: 2027-06-14).

3) Autoscale edge-case & transient RPCs (8m)
- Root pattern: scale-up bursts cause transient registration jitter with the load-balancer leading to RPC retries.
- Short-term mitigations: staggered grow windows + pre-warm signaling from autoscaler.
- Action: Oliver to ship a conservative grow-window patch and a monitor for retry rate anomalies (owner: Oliver Chen, due: 2027-06-11).

4) Observability and cost attribution (6m)
- Problem: dedicated customers using prefix cache show misattributed token counts in billing pipeline. Ruth proposes instrumenting cache-hit token counts at emit point.
- Constraints: must not add high-cardinality tags to span metadata. Use aggregated counters per pool.
- Action: Ruth to provide a lightweight schema and ingestion estimate (owner: Ruth Alvarez, due: 2027-06-12).

Open blockers and cross-team asks:
- Solutions/customer readiness: Irene needs a short checklist for private deploys that includes kernel-compatibility matrix and KMS smoke tests. Maya and Samir to provide inputs (owners: Maya Singh & Samir Patel, due: 2027-06-13).
- Legal/compliance note: a partner requires FIPS-compatible crypto verification on a private stack; outline to legal to be provided by platform (owner: Ethan Morales, due: 2027-06-15).

Decisions taken:
- Approve temporary reallocation of 12 A100-equivalent slots from non-prod to prod for 4 weeks (owner: Maya Singh to execute).
- Begin plan to add a customer-facing "latency-pref" routing label in the catalog; prototyping to start next sprint.

Action item summary (single-line):
- Maya Singh: Reallocate 12 slots, produce rollback plan and timeline (due 2027-06-10).
- Oliver Chen: Ship staggered grow-window autoscaler patch + retry anomaly monitor (due 2027-06-11).
- Ruth Alvarez: Observability schema for cache-hit token attribution with ingestion estimate (due 2027-06-12).
- Samir Patel: Draft SDK routing flag + product spec for latency/cost preference (due 2027-06-14).
- Ethan Morales: Coordinate with legal on FIPS ask and confirm partner scope (due 2027-06-15).
- Maya & Samir: Deliver private deploy checklist for solutions team (due 2027-06-13).

Notes to self / meeting artifacts:
- Link experimental data: CONFLUENCE-1488 (packing experiment raw data).
- Keep the condensed non-prod stress window to weekdays 03:00-05:00 UTC while borrowed slots are in use.
- Follow-up: 1:1 with infra procurement to speed order lead time.

Next sync:
- Weekly: 2027-06-15 at 0900 PT. If the autoscaler patch lands early Oliver will call a quick follow-up.

Recorder: Ethan Morales
